description: A procedure body sees ONLY its parameters, the bindings its body has already made, and names declared `global` (spec/execution-model.md:389-394) — every other variable of every enclosing scope is invisible, not merely unwritable. This is that section's own worked example, verbatim: `draw_steps` cannot see the top-level `:count`, so `forward :count * 10` raises `ol-var-not-visible`. The diagnostic fires on the READ because the read comes first (:443-446); had the write come first it would have created a binding in the scope the write appears in, which is a genuinely different variable and correct. Registry stage is `semantic` (the checker decides it lexically, issue #825); the runtime raises it at `stage: "runtime"` because `execute()` never runs `check()`, under the same code and `params` so the two stages report one identity. `params.procedure` is what makes the message name the boundary, which `spec/error-model.md:132` requires of this code specifically.

diagnostics.message: :count is not defined inside draw_steps. a procedure only sees its own inputs, the names it sets itself, and names declared global. the fix is one word at the top level: write global count = (its starting value).
